name: Phoebe Bridgers
label: Dead Oceans
lede: Phoebe Bridgers wrote a debut about grief, smashed a guitar on Saturday Night Live, formed two bands with famous friends, and put out a third album that Pitchfork scored 8.4.

eras.title: A Pasadena kid with a guitar
eras.text: Phoebe Bridgers grew up in Pasadena, picked up a guitar around 13 and made her first money busking. Vocal jazz school and a Berklee place she walked away from came before any of it became a career.

years.h: Pasadena's farmers market gets her first gig
years.p: Her father built sets for film and TV. Bridgers busked at the Pasadena Farmers Market as a kid and started guitar around 13.

years.h: Berklee says yes, and she leaves after orientation
years.p: She began studying vocal jazz at the Los Angeles County High School for the Arts in 2009. Berklee accepted her; she left after orientation.

eras.title: Free studio time and a secret showcase
eras.text: Her first EP came out on Ryan Adams's label, her real debut got made for free, and two tours plus one secret showcase built the circle around her.

years.h: Killer EP comes out on Ryan Adams's label
years.p: [[Ryan Adams|c80f38a6-9980-485d-997c-5c1a9cbd0d64]] released Bridgers's first EP on PAX AM, his own label. Wikipedia says they met through mutual collaborators.

years.h: Tony Berg makes her debut for nothing
years.p: Berg started work on her first album for free. An Apple commercial she made with [[Sloppy Jane|dfa3f308-ca2c-48f8-b866-3392fbfe5bca]] paid for her to finish it before she went looking for a label.

years.h: Lucy Dacus and Bridgers both open for Julien Baker in 2016
years.p: [[Julien Baker|e3bda984-f349-4924-b4b8-f72478bbb3f3]] had just put out Sprained Ankle. Bridgers and [[Lucy Dacus|dbe7fdf7-81b2-418b-b3f6-81ae71532f40]] each opened for her on separate tours, and that's where the three of them got close.

years.cap: Bridgers at a Daytrotter session, June 2016
years.src: Wikipedia: Phoebe Bridgers · Wikipedia: Better Oblivion Community Center
years.h: Conor Oberst throws a private showcase at the Bootleg Theater
years.p: The [[Bright Eyes|78f797e3-4913-4026-aad0-1cd858bd735b]] singer organized the Los Angeles show and Bridgers played it. By January he had her opening his European tour.
years.xp:
Oberst and his Bright Eyes bandmate [[Mike Mogis|0306016b-331c-4519-b51e-f11dfc217455]] later contributed vocals and production to Bridgers's debut, so the showcase turned into a working relationship fast. In 2019 the pair made an album together as [[Better Oblivion Community Center|9861b813-3e8e-4e3a-b5ec-78ac6280489a]].

Sources date the meeting to summer 2016; the Better Oblivion Community Center page says July.

eras.title: The debut lands, and a trio forms
eras.text: A European tour with Conor Oberst, a Dead Oceans deal and a debut about grief and Echo Park loneliness put Bridgers on the map. By the end of 2018 she was also a third of boygenius.

years.h: 'Smoke Signals' goes out, and Europe with Oberst follows
years.p: Bridgers released the single in January 2017 and opened Oberst's European tour that month.

years.cap: Bridgers solo at Theater Roode Bioscope, Amsterdam, July 2017
years.h: Marshall Vore co-writes second single 'Motion Sickness'
years.p: She wrote it with [[Marshall Vore|5bb26424-63ce-432e-aaf5-2bd80fe7a732]]; [[Tony Berg|ca0d305c-f3bc-4684-a117-085e4722aef1]] and [[Ethan Gruska|060be8ed-bd5a-46d6-8660-6b61b19c2a62]] produced. NME ranked it 16th among 2017's best songs, and Pitchfork later put it 64th among the 2010s'.

years.src: Wikipedia: Stranger in the Alps · Wikipedia: Phoebe Bridgers
years.h: Stranger in the Alps takes its title from the TV cut of The Big Lebowski
years.p: Berg and Gruska produced it at Zeitgeist in Brentwood, Los Angeles, after Bridgers signed to Dead Oceans in June.
years.xp:
Bridgers has said she found the phrase poetic by accident. 'Scott Street' is named for Scott Avenue in Echo Park, near a practice space where she and Vore stored gear, and 'Funeral', the last single, was inspired by a close friend's overdose, according to Wikipedia.

Metacritic scored the album 82 from 16 reviews and The A.V. Club gave it a perfect score. It peaked at No. 82 on the Billboard 200 and later went gold in the US and UK.

yt: Phoebe Bridgers: NPR Music Tiny Desk Concert
years.h: Bridgers does her first NPR Tiny Desk
years.p: It was the first of four in different guises: solo, boygenius, Better Oblivion Community Center and, in 2020, from home.

years.cap: Bridgers at the Turf Club, St. Paul, April 2018
years.h: Bridgers, Baker and Dacus announce boygenius
years.p: They put out three songs and a plan for a co-headlining tour.
years.xp:
The three got close after Dacus and Bridgers opened for Baker on separate 2016 tours, and they shared a frustration at being lumped together as women in rock despite very different styles. Baker had joked years earlier about a pipe-dream band.

Dacus has said the name began as a joke about the unearned confidence handed to male artists. The band sometimes writes it as xboygeniusx, a nod to straight-edge punk and to Baker's own past.

years.h: boygenius cut an EP in four days and release it early
years.p: They recorded at Sound City that June with an all-women crew, and Matador put it out two weeks ahead of the scheduled November 9 date.
years.xp:
Each brought a mostly finished song ('Stay Down' from Baker, 'Me & My Dog' from Bridgers, 'Bite the Hand' from Dacus). 'Ketchum, ID' was co-written with [[Christian Lee Hutson|75a7274d-e9f1-4569-be5e-f590ab9ddb64]]. The cover nods to Crosby, Stills & Nash's 1969 debut.

Pitchfork's Dayna Evans scored it 8.3, writing that the members' distinct styles yield 'an effective kind of magic'. NPR Music ranked it 12th among the best albums of 2018. A November US tour included Late Night with Seth Meyers and a Tiny Desk.

eras.title: Better Oblivion, and a reckoning
eras.text: Bridgers spent the year in a duo with Oberst and, in February, answered a New York Times report about Ryan Adams.

years.h: A Replacements joke becomes a band, unveiled on Colbert
years.p: Bridgers and Oberst introduced Better Oblivion Community Center on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert, and the album came out at midnight.
years.xp: The idea started when Bridgers complimented Oberst's cover of a Replacements song, and he suggested they start a band that sounded like the Replacements. She thought he was joking; Oberst dreams up fake bands all the time.

years.h: Better Oblivion Community Center's debut gets a Michelle Zauner video
years.p: Zauner of Japanese Breakfast directed the clip for lead single 'Dylan Thomas'. The duo played CBS This Morning and a Tiny Desk, and their last show was August 11 in San Francisco.

years.src: Variety: Phoebe Bridgers Slams Ryan Adams' 'Network' of Enablers · Rolling Stone: Phoebe Bridgers Issues New Statement Addressing Ryan Adams Allegations · Wikipedia: Ryan Adams
years.h: Seven women go on record about Ryan Adams, Bridgers among them
years.p: The New York Times report of February 13 included Bridgers's account of Adams's conduct. Adams initially denied the accusations.
years.xp:
The Times reported that her relationship with Adams began as a mentorship when she was 20 and turned controlling. Wikipedia notes her 2017 single 'Motion Sickness' addresses their relationship.

Bridgers responded on Instagram, according to Variety: 'Ryan had a network too. Friends, bands, people he worked with. None of them held him accountable.'

eras.title: A pandemic album and one smashed guitar
eras.text: The album arrived in a pandemic and a summer of protests, and touring only caught up a year later. In between she started a label, released an orchestral remix EP and broke one guitar.

q: I'm not delaying the record until things go back to 'normal'.
years.src: Wikipedia: Punisher (Phoebe Bridgers album) · Wikipedia: Phoebe Bridgers
years.h: Punisher lands a day early
years.p: Bridgers moved it up from June 19, Juneteenth, and pointed fans toward racial justice organizations instead.
years.xp:
Berg and Gruska produced at Sound City in Van Nuys, from mid-2018 to late 2019, with Oberst on several tracks. Singles: 'Garden Song' (February 26), 'Kyoto' (April 9), 'ICU' (May 19).

Metacritic scored it 90 and Pitchfork named it Best New Music. It earned four nominations at the 63rd Grammys: Best New Artist, Best Rock Performance, Best Rock Song and Best Alternative Music Album. A remix EP with [[Rob Moose|c359f7ee-cbcb-4cff-97e0-c1d944b97080]], Copycat Killer, followed on November 20.

years.h: Four guests pile onto 'I Know the End'
years.p: That's Bridgers's own description of the fourth single, which builds from a hush to a huge finish. Baker, Dacus, Oberst and [[Nick Zinner|20dc35ec-6cc1-4c66-98a3-4a6116cb3869]] of the Yeah Yeah Yeahs all appear on it.
years.xp: The video, directed by Alissa Torvinen, ends at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Vulture ranked it the best song of 2020; Consequence of Sound and The Ringer each put it second.

years.h: With The 1975 tour cancelled, Bridgers plays Tiny Desk from home
years.p: NPR's home version of the series gave 'I Know the End' its live debut, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Saddest Factory opens, named by a Twitter suggestion
years.p: Bridgers started the imprint under Dead Oceans. [[Haley Dahl|274937a1-9e48-4a00-9fea-53eebfa7f616]] of Sloppy Jane suggested the name, a riff on 'satisfactory', and [[Claud|34f3e890-c917-4ee1-b859-b22c48e2a42c]] was the first signing.
years.xp:
The roster grew to include Muna, Sloppy Jane, Charlie Hickey, Katie Gavin and Jasmine.4.T, with releases including Claud's Super Monster (2021) and Muna's self-titled album (2022).

Wikipedia cites a June 16, 2026 Pitchfork report that Saddest Factory was merging into Dead Oceans, following a trademark dispute.

years.big: "It's hilarious to me that people care"
years.src: NME: Watch Phoebe Bridgers smash her guitar · Tone Deaf: Phoebe Bridgers reflects on her 'SNL' guitar smash · Rolling Stone: Phoebe Bridgers on 'SNL'
years.h: Bridgers ends her SNL set by smashing a guitar into a monitor
years.p: She played 'Kyoto' and 'I Know the End' on Saturday Night Live and finished the second by wrecking her guitar. That's what she told Tone Deaf about the reaction.
years.xp: Rolling Stone's headline read 'Yes, It's OK for Women to Smash Guitars', and NME called it her 'explosive' SNL debut. DragonForce guitarist Herman Li made a reaction video.

years.cap: Bridgers on guitar at Shaky Knees, Atlanta, October 2021
years.h: Everyone wants a Bridgers verse
years.p: In 2021 she sang on [[Lorde|8e494408-8620-4c6a-82c2-c2ca4a1e4f12]]'s Solar Power, joined The Killers on 'Runaway Horses', guested on Muna's 'Silk Chiffon' and covered Bo Burnham's 'That Funny Feeling'.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, she sang background on five Solar Power tracks in August, 'Silk Chiffon' came out on September 7, and her 'That Funny Feeling' cover reached No. 2 on the Rock & Alternative chart in October. In November she sang 'Nothing New' with Taylor Swift on Red (Taylor's Version).

years.cap: Bridgers at Marymoor Park, Redmond, Washington, August 2022
years.h: St. Louis starts a Reunion Tour that runs 106 shows
years.p: It ended on April 26, 2023 in Murfreesboro, Tennessee. Her Saddest Factory roster opened her 2022 North American dates.
years.xp: Muna and Bartees Strange supported early dates, with Baker sitting in at Berkeley. Red Rocks was on May 17, 2022, with Sloppy Jane opening. A Bonnaroo date on September 4, 2021 was cancelled after Hurricane Ida flooding.

years.h: boygenius headline a benefit, their first full set since 2018
years.p: The Bread and Roses benefit was in San Francisco. In July 2020 they'd released demos on Bandcamp that raised $23,000 for charities.

eras.title: boygenius make the record, then walk away
eras.text: boygenius made a full album, won three Grammys with it and then announced a hiatus in the same week.

years.h: The Record goes to No. 1 in the UK, Ireland and the Netherlands
years.p: boygenius recorded it at Shangri-La in Malibu and Sound City with Catherine Marks, and put it out on Interscope.
years.xp:
Kristen Stewart directed the videos for '$20', 'True Blue' and 'Emily I'm Sorry'. Pitchfork scored it 8.2, and it peaked at No. 4 on the Billboard 200. The vinyl B-side of 'Letter to an Old Poet' ends in a locked groove that repeats the word 'waiting'.

They played Coachella in April, released the The Rest EP on October 13 and performed on Saturday Night Live on November 11 with host Timothée Chalamet.

years.cap: boygenius (Bridgers, Baker and Dacus) at PRYZM, Kingston, UK, August 2023
years.h: boygenius go on indefinite hiatus at a secret Los Angeles show
years.p: The band said it wasn't a breakup. Dacus later said she was 'not convinced' the hiatus would be permanent.
years.xp: The announcement came in the same week as the Grammys, where the band won three awards.

years.cap: boygenius on stage in Redmond, Washington, July 2023
years.h: Bridgers leaves the Grammys with four wins
years.p: boygenius won Best Alternative Music Album, Best Rock Song ('Not Strong Enough') and Best Rock Performance. The fourth came for SZA's 'Ghost in the Machine', which features Bridgers.

eras.title: Lost Weekend
eras.text: Six years after Punisher, Bridgers announced her third album with phone-free shows instead of interviews, then a Renaissance-fair video and a guest list that includes both of her boygenius bandmates. Pitchfork gave it 8.4.

years.src: Variety: Phoebe Bridgers Turns Madison Square Garden · Wikipedia: Phoebe Bridgers · Wikipedia: Lost Weekend
years.h: A phone-free Madison Square Garden, with tickets at $1 to $20
years.p: Variety called it possibly the biggest phone-free concert ever, and counted eight new songs.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, proceeds went to the Community Justice Exchange's Immigration Bond Freedom Fund. In May she had played short-notice shows in Roswell, New Mexico, Lubbock and Little Rock with recording devices banned.

On June 5 she announced The Lost Tour of North America and Europe for September to December, with Alex G and Isaac Wood as openers.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lost Boys · Variety: Phoebe Bridgers Stars in Renaissance Faire-Themed
years.h: Bridgers plays an elf at a Renaissance fair in 'Lost Boys'
years.p: Lance Oppenheim and Pablo Rochat directed Bridgers as an elf leading knights at a LARP event, with Skyler Gisondo as a smitten convenience-store clerk.
years.xp:
The song was written with Christian Lee Hutson, Marshall Vore, Bo Burnham and [[Alex G|7df4c4de-3181-4a69-bd36-9d663970cebb]], and Under the Radar lists Baker, Dacus and Alex G as features. It topped US Adult Alternative Airplay and reached No. 85 on the Hot 100.

Wikipedia records mixed reviews: Consequence called it a comeback single, while Pitchfork found the lyrics leaned on cliché.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lost Weekend · NPR: On 'Lost Weekend,' · Stereogum: Premature Evaluation · Pop Base: Pitchfork gives
years.h: Lost Weekend gets an 8.4 from Pitchfork
years.p: It runs sixteen tracks, produced by Bridgers, Gruska, [[Jack Antonoff|1155a7a9-a7b4-46ba-ba27-6b6c98be487e]], Berg and [[Alex G|7df4c4de-3181-4a69-bd36-9d663970cebb]].
years.xp:
Guests include Baker, Dacus, Burnham (seven co-writing credits, per NPR), [[Maya Hawke|6879c573-d161-427c-8b67-77d65fa477bb]], Justin Broadrick, Caroline Shaw, Blake Mills and Mike Kinsella. 'Never Going Back!' includes a voicemail from her father, Stereogum reports, and NPR's Ann Powers writes that Bridgers pulls at her memories 'like Silly Putty'.

Recording ran 2022 to 2026, and the album deals with her father's death. Metacritic scored it 91, and it went to No. 1 in the UK, Ireland, Australia and New Zealand and No. 2 on the Billboard 200, per Wikipedia.
